feature_notes:
Adds usable configurable ZIP compression: WriteOptions and SaveOptions expose validated optional levels; WorkbookWriter can set the packaging level without respooling. None preserves default level 6, 1 through 9 use Deflate, and 0 stores rewritten ZIP parts without compression. Invalid options reject before output; unchanged editor entries preserve their original compressed bytes.

Default backend is explicitly pure-Rust zlib-rs, which the former zip deflate feature already used. Optional deflate-zlib enables native zlib when built with no default features; it needs a C toolchain. Unused Zopfli support is removed. Backend choice is compile-time, not a runtime workbook setting.

Representative one-million-cell Linux Rust 1.99 measurements: zlib-rs numeric creation level 6 takes 0.9200 s / 2,942,935 ZIP bytes; level 3 takes 0.2487 s / 3,299,121 bytes. Existing A1 edit/save is 1.3052 s at level 6 versus 0.7529 s at level 3 with nearly unchanged ZIP size. Native zlib is not universally faster; higher levels do not guarantee smaller files. Raw samples and complete uncompressed-part hash/CRC agreement across numeric, mixed and editing workloads are recorded in benchmarks/alpha4-compression.md.

Both backends pass Rust 1.88 on Windows and Linux; formatting, strict Clippy, documentation and workspace tests pass. Resource limits, formula-cache invalidation, original assets and atomic output protection remain intact. Worksheet spools and full temporary output ZIP costs remain documented. Test consolidation and M2 completion/closure move to alpha.5; M2 remains open.
